entry.title: ARC-Impute: robust reference-guided spatial gene imputation through regularised cell-to-spot mapping
entry.summary:
Motivation: Reference-guided spatial imputation uses single-cell RNA sequencing references to predict genes that are unmeasured in spatial transcriptomics data. Limited shared-gene overlap can leave the mapping of reference cells to spatial locations ambiguous: different assignments may reconstruct observed genes similarly yet yield different imputed expression and cell-type estimates. This gives rise to local assignment ambiguity, source-target mismatch and reference-transfer instability.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: MitoArc: A Reproducible Short-Read Workflow for Human Mitochondrial Genome Analysis with Circular-Coordinate and NUMT-Aware Evaluation
entry.summary:
Human mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) analysis from short-read sequencing is complicated by nuclear mitochondrial DNA segments (NUMTs), circular-reference coordinates, sequencing depth, and variant-caller configuration. We developed MitoArc, a Nextflow workflow that accepts paired-end FASTQ files or pre-aligned BAM and CRAM files, retains available nuclear mapping context, and performs standard and shifted-coordinate processing. It runs Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) Mutect2 and mutserve2 independently and reports mitochondrial quality metrics, NUMT evidence, haplogroups, contamination estimates, functional annotations, consensus sequences, and reproducibility outputs.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #consensus

entry.title: An alternative path for artificial intelligence in Africa
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01084-9 African governments face a perceived choice between investing in costly national data centers and dependence on foreign technology providers. Both options rest on assumptions that the evidence no longer supports. We argue for a third path, distributed sovereignty: cooperative infrastructure designed for African conditions.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #distributed-systems

entry.title: Generative molecular design needs oracle grounding
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01082-x Generative molecular design is guided by oracles, computational proxies of experimental goals that models can exploit. We argue that oracle grounding, in which experiments diagnose and correct oracle failures, will allow generative models to discover not only new molecules but also new chemistry.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #infosec

entry.title: Minimizing data requirements for chemical and material property prediction via cluster-based training set selection
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01076-9 A survey of 100 algorithms across 60 chemical and materials property prediction tasks finds that cluster-based selection of training data outperforms active learning, and a theoretical framework establishes why this occurs in the low-data limit.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science
